title: hbs-state: index guard for stateful hash-based signatures (XMSS/XMSS^MT)
description:
Index guard for stateful hash-based signatures (XMSS/XMSS^MT): a monotonic counter persisted with fsync, detection of storage that does not actually persist, and reconciliation of the state after a restart. Reference implementation of HBS-STATE.

This release is crate version 0.1.0 and it implements specification HBS-STATE v0.3, which is archived alongside it under spec/. The two version numbers are independent: the crate versions the implementation, the specification versions the contract.

NIST SP 800-208 approves stateful hash-based signatures and at the same time requires key and signature generation to be validated only inside hardware modules, because the security depends on state management. RFC 10033 demands the four ACID properties over that state and gives nine state-management strategies, and not one of the nine ships a single executable vector. This crate is the reference implementation of a minimal specification of one property -- how you decide, after a restart, whether the state is still safe to use -- with four states, one judge, and numeric vectors any implementation can consume, plus the verifier and the reference subject that turn an implementation into something the bench can measure. Zero dependencies.
